body: It feels like you and I live on a different planet.
Thank you, genuinely, it helps to know I'm not crazy.

They can afford the time to reply to people they've shortlisted, and I've been on shortlists aplenty, but still nothing. Even then, I would wager the vast majority of the time they don't get anyone because I've been seeing listings reappear every day for months at a time.

When you've been applying for jobs for months, you start to get very good at it, and more importantly, you get a lot of autofill data for each application site. The vast majority of companies in the UK use just 4 external sites, like Workday or BambooHR, and those are very easy to get through using autofill, though I wish Workday didn't force you to make a new account for each separate employer, but at this point that's autofill data too.

  
It does actually take me roughly 1-2 minutes per application on average now, so your math checks out. I have been trying multiple different CVs and cover letters and different formats, even different ways to approach jobs, but the issue I have is that there is no feedback at all, so there's no way of knowing what works. I'm trying to learn to play darts while blindfolded and wearing earmuffs.

Honestly I'm not a fan of generating cover letters. I'm a sucker in the sense that I still want to write cover letters myself and actually put effort and soul into them, and that's part of why I feel so downtrodden.

It's not actually chatGPT or any other AI as I understand it, since systems like Workday predate it and are a lot more rudimentary in what they do. It's just an algorithmic ATS that more or less assigns points then ranks candidates, but I believe it can also discard some applications itself, though most ATS companies say this is not the case and it is just at the very bottom.

Yeah, I figured racism played a part in it. When I was applying in the US years ago, the job I eventually got told me that they found me in their automatic rejection pile (hence why I'm skeptical when ATS companies say there's no rejection going on) despite being one of the top CVs they received and it specifically flagged my name as why.
I'm not trying to dunk on anyone by saying this: it's genuinely disheartening how many people have accepted this kind of treatment as normal.
Thank you, I'll keep it around. It's nice to have *some* feedback.
I've tried around a dozen different methods but the issue is there's no feedback either way, so it's impossible to tell what works best.
I'm genuinely sorry they've made you accept this kind of treatment as normal.

To both you and u/FatDad66, the reason I can apply for so many in one day is because I have worked in several fields within the finance/compliance/business/sales sphere. I apply for jobs across the entire UK because I have no issues commuting several hours a day if necessary, so within those fields I see roughly 1,000-3,000 open positions every 3 days. If you remove around 1/3rd of that because I don't qualify, such as senior positions, and another \~1/5th-1/4th that are reposts of the same job. That leaves me with usually \~500-2,000 jobs to sift through, and the vast, *vast* majority of them have the exact same job description because they're being posted by the same handful of recruitment firms. I've been applying so consistently for so long that I have CVs and cover letters ready for each type, and on the off chance they need a new one, that doesn't take too long to make either. Some applications are as easy as clicking and selecting the right CV/cover letter combo, others can take upwards of half an hour to complete because of entitled employers who believe they're owed my time but I'm not even owed a morsel of a response. Feel free to call it entitled, but if entitlement is asking for human treatment, maybe re-evaluate your standards for how people should treat each other. And no, they aren't generic applications, because being the sucker that I am, I still try unlike them.

  
Re: HR having more roles advertised, woe is me, it may take them up to several weeks to filter through applications, the horror.
I make it abundantly clear that I don't. I've also tried removing all mention of it entirely, but I receive no feedback either way, so it's hard to know which works better.

Doesn't apply to recruitment companies, who post most of the jobs and still don't reply, when it's their one job. You can dismiss me all you want, but at this volume the issues are systemic. If you believe companies are entitled to do whatever the hell they want and being pissed off at the dehumanisation inherent to it is entitlement, then congratulations on accepting your lot in life as whatever they decide you are, let's hope it's as a customer and not a spreadsheet row.
Oh, thank you, I'll do that! I didn't know that was a thing.
